name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure
snippet: Oracle's cloud rents large GPU clusters to frontier labs, led by OpenAI. It delivered 850 MW of new capacity in the June to August 2026 quarter and reports $664B of remaining performance obligations.
origin: Oracle entered the public cloud market after Amazon, Microsoft and Google, and its OCI platform found a foothold in AI by renting large GPU clusters to model developers. The Stargate partnership with OpenAI turned that business into Oracle's main source of growth. In September 2025 The Wall Street Journal reported that OpenAI agreed to buy about $300B of Oracle computing power over five years starting in 2027, which press reports put at about 4.5 GW.
today: Oracle's remaining performance obligations reached $664B at the end of August 2026, up from $638B at the end of May. In the June to August quarter Oracle delivered 850 MW of data center capacity and more than 300,000 GPUs, and OCI revenue rose 121% to $7.4B. Oracle reported 97.9% utilization across its multi-tenant GPU fleet. It said it has handed over 618 MW across six of the eight buildings at the Abilene, Texas campus it runs for OpenAI. Oracle booked more than $30B of new AI contracts in the quarter, and most of them carry customer prepayments or customer-supplied hardware. Earlier commitments came from OpenAI, Meta and NVIDIA, and Oracle said in June 2026 that prepaid and customer-supplied hardware in its large AI contracts totals $75B.
platform: OCI sells NVIDIA and AMD GPUs as bare-metal and virtual machine instances, grouped into Superclusters that Oracle says scale to 131,072 GPUs. Its Zettascale10 design, announced in October 2025, uses Oracle's Acceleron RoCE network with multiple isolated planes to link GPUs across data centers within about two kilometers, with initial deployments of up to 800,000 NVIDIA GPUs. OpenAI's Abilene site with OCI runs MRC, a multipath RDMA transport that OpenAI developed with Microsoft, AMD, Broadcom and NVIDIA for two-tier multiplane networks of up to 131,072 GPUs. Oracle also offers AMD Instinct MI300X and MI355X instances and plans a 50,000-GPU MI450 cluster starting in the third quarter of 2026.
outlook: Oracle funds its build-out with debt, equity and customer prepayments, and said in February 2026 it planned to raise $45B to $50B that year through a bond offering and an equity program. In the June to August 2026 quarter it spent $28.5B on capex and received $11.4B of customer prepayments. Oracle guides fiscal 2027 capex to $90B to $95B, with no more than $70B of net cash capex. It says its New Mexico and Wisconsin sites are on track, while the New Mexico site still needs air permits for on-site fuel cell power.

name: Google Cloud
snippet: Google's public cloud rents its own TPUs alongside NVIDIA GPUs. Its backlog reached $514B in June 2026, and Google now also sells TPUs to labs and neoclouds for their own data centers.
origin: Google opened its infrastructure to outside developers with App Engine in 2008 and grew that business into Google Cloud. Google designed the Tensor Processing Unit for its own services and later rented TPUs to cloud customers. That in-house chip line gives Google Cloud a second source of AI accelerators next to NVIDIA GPUs.
today: Google Cloud revenue grew 82% to $24.8B in the second quarter of 2026, and its backlog rose by more than $50B in the quarter to $514B. Anthropic, which secured access to up to 1 million TPUs in October 2025, signed in April 2026 for about 3.5 GW of next-generation TPU capacity from Google and Broadcom starting in 2027. Meta signed a multibillion-dollar deal to rent TPUs in February 2026. Thinking Machines Lab signed a multibillion-dollar contract for NVIDIA GB300 capacity on Google Cloud in April 2026. Google said in April 2026 that it would deliver TPUs to a select group of customers for their own data centers, and Blackstone committed $5B of equity in May 2026 to a separate TPU cloud that targets 500 MW by 2027. Google backstops Fluidstack lease obligations at TeraWulf sites, which places TPU capacity in third-party data centers. In March 2026 Google closed its $32B purchase of Wiz and its $4.75B purchase of the energy developer Intersect.
platform: Google sells TPUs and NVIDIA GPUs through its AI Hypercomputer stack, with Ironwood (TPU7x) pods of up to 9,216 chips and A4, A4X and A4X Max virtual machines for B200, GB200 and GB300. At Cloud Next in April 2026 it announced the TPU 8t for training, the TPU 8i for inference, A5X bare-metal instances on NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72, and the Virgo network fabric for very large clusters. Cluster Director, generally available since December 2025, runs managed Slurm clusters alongside GKE. Since July 2026 NVIDIA's NGC containers include Google's gIB NCCL plugins, which configure themselves on Google Cloud GPU machines.
outlook: Google plans to sell TPUs outside its own cloud through direct hardware sales, the Blackstone venture and neocloud partners, which puts it in competition with the neoclouds it supplies. Sundar Pichai said revenue from TPU sales into customer data centers begins in 2026, with a larger effect in 2027. Meta has reportedly discussed buying TPUs for its own data centers from 2027. Google expects to recognize just over 50% of its $514B backlog as revenue within 24 months.

name: Microsoft Azure
snippet: Microsoft's cloud runs much of OpenAI's compute and sells AI capacity to Anthropic and enterprises. Azure grew 43% in the June 2026 quarter, and commercial backlog reached $678B.
origin: Microsoft launched Azure in 2010 as its general-purpose public cloud. Its AI accelerator business grew out of its partnership with OpenAI, for which Azure built and ran large training supercomputers. Microsoft held rights to OpenAI's compute until an October 2025 restructuring removed its right of first refusal.
today: Azure revenue grew 43% in the quarter that ended June 2026, and Microsoft said customer demand still exceeds available capacity. Commercial remaining performance obligations rose 84% to $678B. In October 2025 OpenAI contracted to buy an incremental $250B of Azure services. Anthropic committed in November 2025 to buy $30B of Azure compute and to contract up to 1 GW more on NVIDIA Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin systems. Microsoft also buys capacity from neoclouds, including a multibillion-dollar Nebius contract at Vineland, New Jersey and a deployment that IREN said it delivered in August 2026. Capex reached $41B in the June 2026 quarter, and roughly two thirds of it went to short-lived assets, mainly CPUs and GPUs.
platform: Microsoft's Fairwater AI data centers in Wisconsin and Atlanta link hundreds of thousands of NVIDIA GB200 and GB300 GPUs over a two-tier Ethernet back-end network and a dedicated AI WAN, with racks at about 140 kW. Microsoft engineers co-developed MRC, a multipath RDMA transport that runs in OpenAI's and Microsoft's largest training clusters. Maia 200, a TSMC 3 nm inference chip with 216 GB of HBM3e, entered production in January 2026 and serves Copilot and OpenAI models. Customers reach models through Microsoft Foundry and GPUs through Azure virtual machines and Kubernetes.
outlook: Microsoft plans to scale Maia to multi-gigawatt deployments starting in 2027, with Maia 300 on TSMC N2P as the main inference system for its own products. Microsoft said all sequential growth in commercial RPO in the June 2026 quarter came from customers outside frontier model companies. Capacity remains the limit on Azure AI revenue, since Microsoft says demand exceeds supply.

name: Amazon Web Services
snippet: Amazon's cloud pairs NVIDIA GPUs with its own Trainium chips. AWS grew 37% to $42.2B in the June 2026 quarter, and Anthropic and OpenAI have made multi-gigawatt Trainium commitments.
origin: Amazon launched AWS in 2006 and built it into the largest public cloud. Its Annapurna Labs unit designs custom chips, including the Trainium line for model training and inference. Amazon's investment in Anthropic made the lab the anchor customer for Trainium.
today: AWS revenue rose 37% to $42.2B in the second quarter of 2026, its fastest growth in 18 quarters. Both Amazon's AI business and its chips business passed $25B annual run rates. Amazon said in April 2026 that Anthropic will secure up to 5 GW of current and future Trainium chips and that OpenAI committed to about 2 GW of Trainium capacity. Those deals add to the $38B, seven-year contract OpenAI signed in November 2025 for NVIDIA GB200 and GB300 capacity, which AWS targets to deploy before the end of 2026. Project Rainier, the Anthropic cluster that includes sites in Indiana, runs more than 500,000 Trainium2 chips. Amazon landed more than 2.1 million AI chips in the 12 months before its April 2026 report, more than half of them Trainium, and plans about $200B of capex in 2026.
platform: AWS rents GPUs and Trainium through EC2 instances and UltraServers, with its Elastic Fabric Adapter network carrying cluster traffic. Trn3 UltraServers hold up to 144 Trainium3 chips on a 3 nm process, which AWS says deliver up to 4.4 times the compute of Trainium2. Trainium4, planned for 2027, will support NVIDIA NVLink Fusion so Trainium and GPU servers can share MGX racks. Customers train and serve models through SageMaker HyperPod and Amazon Bedrock, which offers models from Anthropic, OpenAI and others.
outlook: AWS said in February 2026 that it expected nearly all Trainium3 supply to be committed by mid-2026, so the Trainium4 ramp in 2027 sets how much new custom-silicon capacity it can sell. AWS competes with neoclouds mainly on Trainium price-performance and on dedicated capacity for frontier labs. Amazon also announced more than 1 million NVIDIA GPUs to be deployed starting in 2026. Its trailing twelve-month free cash flow was negative $7.6B at the end of June 2026 as capex rose.

name: IBM Cloud
snippet: IBM's public cloud targets enterprise and regulated workloads. It rents NVIDIA GPUs up to Blackwell Ultra, AMD Instinct MI300X and Intel Gaudi 3, with up to eight accelerators per virtual server.
origin: IBM Cloud is the public cloud arm of IBM's hybrid cloud strategy, which pairs it with Red Hat OpenShift and the watsonx AI platform. Its GPU business serves enterprises that want to run AI next to IBM software and inside IBM's security and compliance controls.
today: IBM Cloud lists NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs as available, alongside AMD Instinct MI300X and Intel Gaudi 3 accelerators. Its VPC virtual server profiles run up to eight NVIDIA H100, H200 or Gaudi 3 accelerators per instance, with smaller L4, L40S and A100 options. IBM does not publish GPU counts or AI capacity in megawatts.
platform: Customers deploy GPU instances in IBM Cloud VPC or through Red Hat OpenShift, and use IBM watsonx for model development and serving. IBM also offers spot pricing on selected GPUs.

name: Alibaba Cloud
ownership: Subsidiary of Alibaba Group (NYSE: BABA, HKEX: 9988)
snippet: China's largest cloud provider builds its own AI chips through T-Head and serves its Qwen models. Cloud revenue grew 45% in the June 2026 quarter, and Alibaba raised HK$80B in August 2026 for AI infrastructure.
origin: Alibaba founded Alibaba Cloud in 2009 to run its own e-commerce systems and to sell computing to outside customers. It grew into the largest cloud provider in China and opened regions abroad. Alibaba also designs AI chips through its T-Head unit and trains the Qwen family of open-weight models, which it serves on its cloud.
today: Alibaba's cloud revenue rose 45% to RMB 48.4B ($7.1B) in the quarter that ended June 2026, and AI-related product revenue reached RMB 12.4B ($1.8B). Quarterly capex rose 75% to RMB 67.7B ($10.0B), which Alibaba attributes to procurement timing, added compute capacity and higher chip component prices. In August 2026 Alibaba placed 710 million new shares for HK$80B (about $10.3B) and said it will spend the proceeds on AI infrastructure, including global computing capacity and hyperscale AI data centers. T-Head's Zhenwu AI chips now serve more than 650 external customers through Alibaba Cloud. Alibaba announced in February 2025 a plan to spend more than RMB 380B on cloud and AI infrastructure over three years.
platform: Alibaba Cloud sells GPU and in-house accelerator instances, a machine learning platform for training and serving, and API access to Qwen and other models. It operates 29 regions and 87 availability zones worldwide.
outlook: US export controls limit Alibaba's access to NVIDIA's most advanced GPUs, which makes the T-Head chip line central to its capacity growth. Alibaba plans to use the August 2026 placement proceeds to expand computing infrastructure in China and abroad. Higher chip component prices already push up its capex.

name: BytePlus
snippet: ByteDance's international enterprise cloud sells GPU compute, Kubernetes and API access to ByteDance's Seed models through its ModelArk platform.
origin: ByteDance set up BytePlus in 2021 as the international counterpart to Volcano Engine, its enterprise technology brand in China. Its early products included the recommendation technology that ByteDance uses in its own apps. BytePlus now packages ByteDance's AI models and cloud infrastructure for enterprise customers outside China.
today: BytePlus sells a GPU Compute Service, elastic compute, Kubernetes, storage and database services. Its ModelArk platform gives API access to ByteDance's Seed models, including Seedance for video and Seedream for images. Its website lists a Southeast Asia region, and BytePlus does not publish GPU counts or capacity figures.
platform: ModelArk serves several model families through one API, while AgentKit, ServingKit and TrainingKit cover agent building, inference optimization and model development. BytePlus keeps enterprise data separate from ByteDance's consumer apps such as TikTok and holds ISO 27001, SOC 2 and PCI DSS certifications.

name: Akamai Cloud
accelerators: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition
snippet: Akamai turned its CDN and the Linode cloud it bought in 2022 into a distributed AI inference cloud. It signed over $2.8B of multi-year cloud contracts in 2026, including $1.8B from a frontier model provider.
origin: Akamai built one of the first large content delivery networks. It bought the developer cloud Linode for about $900M in March 2022 to add general compute to its edge network. In October 2025 it launched Akamai Inference Cloud with NVIDIA, starting in 20 locations with NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell servers and BlueField-3 DPUs.
today: Akamai's Cloud Infrastructure Services revenue grew 39% to $99M in the second quarter of 2026, out of $1.1B in total revenue. In May 2026 Akamai said a leading US frontier model provider committed $1.8B over seven years to its cloud infrastructure. By August it had signed multi-year cloud contracts worth more than $2.8B in 2026, including more than $600M over four years from a new US technology customer for robotics development.
platform: Akamai Inference Cloud runs NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs with NVIDIA AI Enterprise software and NIM microservices, aimed at low-latency inference close to users. A Kubernetes-based developer platform ships with vLLM, KServe and NVIDIA Dynamo, and Akamai charges no egress fees. The service sits on an edge network that Akamai says spans more than 4,350 points of presence.
outlook: Akamai said at launch that an expanded rollout beyond the first 20 Inference Cloud locations was underway. Cloud infrastructure revenue grows much faster than Akamai's total revenue, which it guides to $4.445B to $4.530B for 2026, but still makes up less than 10% of it.

name: SpaceX (xAI)
ownership: Private (SpaceX filed an S-1 in May 2026)
snippet: xAI, now part of SpaceX, runs the Colossus GPU clusters in Memphis. It rents all of Colossus 1 to Anthropic and sells capacity to Google, so it competes as a compute seller as well as a lab.
origin: Elon Musk founded xAI in 2023 to build the Grok models. It built its first Colossus cluster in a former Electrolux factory in South Memphis, Tennessee, with about 100,000 NVIDIA H100 GPUs finished in 122 days in 2024. SpaceX acquired xAI in an all-stock deal announced in February 2026 that valued xAI at $250B and SpaceX at $1T. xAI later rebranded as SpaceXAI.
today: Colossus 2 in Memphis had 110,000 NVIDIA GB200 and 440,000 GB300 GPUs running in late September 2026, and Musk said the chip count may more than double by year end. Epoch AI estimates the site at about 946 MW as of June 2026, with gas turbines across the state line in Southaven, Mississippi. In May 2026 Anthropic agreed to rent all of Colossus 1, which holds more than 220,000 NVIDIA GPUs and over 300 MW of compute. In June 2026 Google agreed to pay SpaceX about $920M a month for compute at xAI data centers, and Reflection AI signed its own compute deal the same month. SpaceX filed an S-1 registration statement with the SEC in May 2026.
platform: xAI runs its clusters for Grok training and inference and leases whole sites or large GPU blocks to other labs. It sells Grok models through an API. Its Memphis sites draw on on-site gas turbines and Tesla Megapack batteries alongside grid power.
outlook: Musk has said he wants about 1 million GPUs in Memphis, and xAI bought a third building in late 2025 to expand toward nearly 2 GW. Its use of gas turbines without federal air permits drew a lawsuit and regulatory scrutiny, and an agreement with state regulators schedules removal of the temporary turbines by mid-2027. The Anthropic and Google leases make SpaceX a seller of AI capacity, which is why it appears in this guide.

name: Mistral AI
snippet: The French AI lab builds Mistral Compute, a European AI cloud, and targets 1 GW of European capacity by 2030. It raised €3B at a valuation above €21B in September 2026.
origin: Mistral AI started in Paris in 2023 to build open-weight language models. In June 2025 it announced Mistral Compute with NVIDIA, a European AI cloud that offers tens of thousands of GPUs as anything from bare-metal servers to fully managed services. ASML led a €1.7B round in September 2025 that valued Mistral at €11.7B.
today: Mistral raised €3B in September 2026 at a post-money valuation above €21B, led by Samsung Electronics with EQT's Scaleup Europe Fund and PSG Equity. It said part of the money will scale its compute capacity. In August 2026 it set a goal of up to 1 GW of European compute by 2030 and said Amadeus, ASML, Capgemini, Caisse des Dépôts and CMA CGM are making multi-year capacity commitments through European Compute Units. Mistral also signed a collaboration worth hundreds of millions of euros with Saudi Arabia's HUMAIN in August 2026, which includes possible use of HUMAIN data centers. It opened a Munich hub in September 2026 to work with German industry.
platform: Mistral Compute bundles GPUs, orchestration, APIs and Mistral's own products, sold from bare-metal servers up to fully managed platform services. Regional endpoints, generally available since August 2026, keep data and processing in Europe or the US, and a Priority Tier adds committed service levels. Mistral now also serves third-party open models, starting with Z.ai's GLM-5.2, under the same regional controls.
outlook: Mistral's 2026 announcements set the 1 GW target for 2030 but do not name the sites or power contracts behind it. Mistral still uses outside capacity, and it trains models with NVIDIA on DGX Cloud under a March 2026 partnership. Its sovereign European positioning competes with US hyperscaler regions in Europe and with European neoclouds.

name: Groq
snippet: Groq runs GroqCloud, an inference API on its own LPU chips. After licensing its technology to NVIDIA in December 2025, it raised $1B in 2026 and plans to grow from 54 MW to over 200 MW in 2027.
origin: Jonathan Ross founded Groq in 2016 to build the Language Processing Unit, a chip designed for fast inference. Groq sold access to LPUs through the GroqCloud API and built clusters in the US, Saudi Arabia, Finland and Australia. In February 2025 Saudi Arabia announced a $1.5B commitment to expand Groq inference capacity, building on a Dammam cluster brought online in December 2024.
today: In December 2025 Groq signed a non-exclusive licensing agreement with NVIDIA for its inference technology, and founder Jonathan Ross, president Sunny Madra and other staff joined NVIDIA. GroqCloud kept operating as an independent company. Groq raised $650M in June 2026 and a $350M Series A in August 2026 at a $3.5B valuation, led by Disruptive with planned NVIDIA participation. It runs 13 data centers across North America, Europe, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific with 54 MW of capacity and plans more than 200 MW in 2027. Groq became an NVIDIA Cloud Partner in August 2026.
platform: GroqCloud sells token-based API access to open models running on Groq LPUs, and Groq says about 6 million developers use it. In August 2026 Groq said it is among the first to deploy NVIDIA Groq 3 LPX, an inference accelerator that extends Vera Rubin NVL72 systems, working with Dell. Groq also powers HUMAIN One, an enterprise AI operating system from Saudi Arabia's HUMAIN.
outlook: Groq now deploys NVIDIA systems alongside its own LPUs, and its 2027 target of more than 200 MW needs new sites and power. Groq has changed chief executives since the NVIDIA deal, from Simon Edwards in December 2025 to Adam Winter by June 2026.

editor_notes: Seed called the NVIDIA deal a licensing and acqui-hire worth about $20B. Groq's August 2026 release calls the $350M round a Series A even though it follows the $650M June raise. The Saudi data center is the Dammam cluster announced with Aramco leaders. HUMAIN is a platform customer (HUMAIN One), not the site owner as far as verified. HQ and founding year come from general knowledge.
